node-3.label: Current illness began 1 month prior to admission with asymptomatic green-yellow welts and swelling of the glans penis; the swelling became progressively painful and evolved to the size of an orange over 4 days

node-5.label: Physical examination showed grossly edematous glans penis and corona, with a 3.7 x 3.3-cm tender, firm ulcer on the ventral surface of the penis with overlying black eschar, adherent yellow crust, and granulation tissue; no urethral discharge was present

Expert analyses confirm that the biopsy reveals a clonal B-cell infiltrate rather than an infectious/inflammatory process, and the lesion was refractory to multiple antimicrobials. This further refutes an infectious/inflammatory ulcer, so confidence is reduced from 0.05 to 0.02.

Both expert analyses confirm systemic B-cell lymphoma from the clonal CD20+, CD79a+, CD5+ B-cell infiltrate and PET-CT FDG-avid abdominal/peripancreatic nodes. Although bone marrow, flow cytometry, and LDH were unavailable, the experts state these are not needed to support the diagnosis. Confidence increases from 0.9 to 0.95.
